annotations.text:
The screen you have, with the gaps filled: instructions, equipment, demo, and reps that are actually recorded.

Tradeoff: safest, least distinctive. It fixes the drill page without deciding what a drill page should be.

Counting IS the log. Two big targets, one tap per swing, a grid you can correct afterwards.

Tradeoff: only fits drills where an attempt is good or bad. Useless for a hold or a tempo drill.

Video is the page. You watch before you touch anything, and the three cues sit under it.

Tradeoff: dead weight on the fiftieth rep of a drill they already know.

Coaching cues as a checklist the athlete ticks as they feel each one. Turns a hold into something with a task.

Tradeoff: ticking a box is not evidence. Easy to tap through without doing it.

Tap where the ball finished. Location is what an inside-pitch drill is actually about, and it reads back as a pattern.

Tradeoff: nine taps of precision per set, and only hitting-shaped drills have a zone.

Opens on your history and a number to beat. Answers 'why am I doing this again' before it asks for anything.

Tradeoff: nothing to show the first two or three times, which is exactly when motivation matters most.

One set, arm's length away, readable mid-drill. Everything else is a tap behind it.

Tradeoff: hides the context. Needs one of the other screens behind it, so it is a mode rather than a design.

The coach leads: a voice note, today's one instruction, and your best rep against the demo.

Tradeoff: only as good as the coach's input. Falls back to the bland version when they leave it empty.

The camera work applied to hitting: bat speed, attack angle, swing-by-swing decay.

Tradeoff: none of these numbers are calibrated for a swing yet, and a wrong number read confidently is worse than no number.

No expanding. Every drill and every set on one screen, logging inline, so a coach can run a group through it.

Tradeoff: no room for instructions. Assumes they already know the drills.

A setup step before the drill: what to grab, tee height, where to stand the phone.

Tradeoff: an extra screen between the athlete and the work, every single time.
